content_units: Berlin 12-Month Lease Checklist
Use this as a tenant-side review list before you sign. It is practical guidance for Berlin rentals, not legal advice.
-   Deposit:   How much is the Kaution, when is it due, and can it be paid in   3 monthly installments  ?
-   Utilities:   What exactly is included in the monthly payment, and what will be billed later as   Nebenkosten  ?
-   Rent increases:   Does the lease allow future increases, and is there an   index-linked   or   graduated rent   clause?
-   Notice/term:   Is it a normal open-ended lease with notice rights, or a fixed-term arrangement with limits on ending early?
-   Furnished vs unfurnished:   What furniture/appliances are included, and who is responsible if they break?
-   Records:   What signed papers, payment proof, and move-in evidence should you keep from day one?
Questions to Ask Before Signing
Topic   What to ask the landlord/agent   Why it matters   What to keep

Deposit     How many months' cold rent is the deposit?   Is it held separately? Can I pay it in 3 installments? When and under what conditions is it returned?   In Germany, residential deposits are commonly capped at   3 months of cold rent   and often payable in installments.   Lease clause on deposit, bank transfer receipts, deposit account details

Utility charges     Is the advertised rent warm or cold?   Which costs are included: heating, water, trash, building charges? Which are excluded: electricity, internet, TV/radio fee? How often is the annual utility statement provided?   A low monthly rent can still lead to a large year-end top-up if advance utility payments are underestimated.   Rent breakdown, utility advance amount, annual statements, meter readings

Rent increase clauses     Is there an Indexmiete or Staffelmiete clause?   If yes, how often can rent go up and based on what formula/schedule? Are utility increases separate from rent increases?   Rent can rise under specific clauses even during a 12-month stay. You want the mechanism clear before signing.   Lease pages covering rent adjustment, screenshots/ad copy of original price

Notice periods     Can I terminate with the standard tenant notice period?   Is there a minimum stay or waiver of termination rights? If fixed-term, what is the legal reason for the fixed term? Is subletting allowed with consent?   Some leases limit flexibility through minimum terms or fixed-term wording.   Signed lease, any side agreements, email confirmations about early exit/sublet

Furnished vs unfurnished     Exactly what is included?   Bed, wardrobe, kitchen, washing machine, cookware? Is there a separate furniture surcharge? Who repairs supplied appliances? Is there an inventory list?   Furnished rentals may cost more and create disputes over wear, damage, and replacement.   Inventory list, photos/videos at handover, appliance condition notes

Move-in condition and documents     Will we do a written handover protocol?   Are meter readings and existing defects recorded? Will I receive landlord confirmation of residence registration (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung)?   These records protect your deposit and help with Anmeldung.   Handover protocol, defect photos, meter readings, registration confirmation
Clause-by-Clause Watchouts
Deposit and return
- Ask whether the deposit is based on   cold rent  , not warm rent.
- Confirm the payment schedule in writing if paying in installments.
- Ask how long after move-out the landlord typically settles the deposit and what deductions may be made.
- If any part may be held back for utility reconciliation, ask how that is calculated.
Utilities and extra charges
- Ask for a line-by-line split of:
-   Kaltmiete   (base rent)
-   Nebenkostenvorauszahlung   (utility advance)
- heating/hot water
- electricity
- internet
- Ask to see the   latest utility statement   for the apartment, if available.
- Clarify whether the utility amount is a fixed flat charge or an   advance subject to annual reconciliation  .
Rent increase wording
- Ask: “Is rent fixed for the first 12 months, or can it increase during that period?”
- If   Indexmiete  : ask which index is used and how written notice of increases will be given.
- If   Staffelmiete  : ask for the exact future rent schedule by date and amount.
- Check whether there are any separate clauses for modernization-related increases.
Notice periods and ending the lease
- Ask whether the lease is:
- open-ended
- fixed-term
- open-ended with a   minimum rental period
- Confirm how much notice you must give and by what method.
- Ask whether a replacement tenant is accepted if you need to leave early.
- Check whether there are penalties or ongoing rent obligations after early departure.
Furnished vs unfurnished
- Ask for a full   inventory list   attached to the lease.
- Check if there is a separate charge for furniture or fitted kitchen use.
- Confirm responsibility for:
- appliance repairs
- mattress replacement
- normal wear and tear
- missing items at move-out
- Photograph every room and every included item at handover.
Papers to Keep From Day One
-   Signed lease   and all annexes/house rules
-   Rental listing/ad   showing original rent and stated inclusions
-   Deposit payment proof
-   Monthly rent payment proof
-   Handover protocol   at move-in and move-out
-   Dated photos/videos   of the apartment condition
-   Inventory list   for furnished rentals
-   Meter readings   for electricity, gas, water, heating
-   Wohnungsgeberbestätigung   for Anmeldung
- All landlord/agent emails about:
- repairs
- defects
- promised furniture/appliances
- rent increases
- notice/termination
- deposit return
